{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_ac38eacb3c0b4ad8b674293f","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t![NEEDLE](docs/hero.png)\n2\t\n3\t# 🧵 NEEDLE\n4\t\n5\t[![CI](https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/actions/workflows/ci.yml)\n6\t[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)\n7\t[![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/rust-1.75+-orange.svg)](rust-toolchain.toml)\n8\t[![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-0.2.8-green.svg)](Cargo.toml)\n9\t\n10\t**N**avigates **E**very **E**nqueued **D**eliverable, **L**ogs **E**ffort\n11\t\n12\t> Deterministic bead processing with explicit outcome paths.\n13\t\n14\tNEEDLE is a universal wrapper for headless coding CLI agents. It processes a shared bead queue in deterministic order, dispatching work to any headless CLI (Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Aider) and handling every outcome through an explicit, predefined path.\n15\t\n16\t---\n17\t\n18\t## 🚀 Quickstart\n19\t\n20\t```bash\n21\t# Install the latest release\n22\tcurl -fsSL https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash\n23\t\n24\t# Or build from source\n25\tcargo install --git https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE\n26\t\n27\t# Run a worker against a bead-tracked workspace\n28\tcd /path/to/your/workspace\n29\tneedle run --agent claude --identity alpha\n30\t```\n31\t\n32\tA worker starts, claims the next bead, dispatches to your chosen agent CLI, and loops. Multiple workers can run in parallel against the same workspace — coordination is handled by the shared bead queue (no central orchestrator).\n33\t\n34\tSee [`docs/examples/`](docs/examples/) for end-to-end configurations.\n35\t\n36\t---\n37\t\n38\t## 🧶 What is a bead?\n39\t\n40\tA **bead** is a work item — the unit of work NEEDLE processes. Think of it as a structured task ticket: a title, a body describing the deliverable and acceptance criteria, a status (`open`, `in_progress`, `done`), and optional metadata like priority and dependencies.\n41\t\n42\tBeads live in a **bead store** — a SQLite database (`beads.db`) plus a JSONL checkpoint file (`issues.jsonl`) in a `.beads/` directory inside your project. The `br` CLI manages the bead store: create beads, list them, claim them, close them.\n43\t\n44\t```bash\n45\t# Create a bead\n46\tbr create --title \"Add pagination to search results\" --body \"...\"\n47\t\n48\t# List open beads\n49\tbr list --status open\n50\t\n51\t# NEEDLE does the rest: claims, dispatches, and closes beads automatically\n52\t```\n53\t\n54\tNEEDLE workers read from this store, claim the next available bead atomically, dispatch it to your chosen agent CLI, and close it on success — then loop.\n55\t\n56\t---\n57\t\n58\t## 🤔 Why NEEDLE\n59\t\n60\tExisting agent orchestration tools are built for one of two shapes:\n61\t\n62\t- **Conversational frameworks** (LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI) assume a chat loop with a human-in-the-loop or another LLM. They are bad at headless, long-running, cost-bounded work.\n63\t- **Workflow engines** (Temporal, Argo Workflows, Inngest) assume each step is deterministic code. They are bad at non-deterministic agent steps whose outcomes have to be classified and routed.\n64\t\n65\tNEEDLE is the missing middle: a **deterministic state machine that drives non-deterministic agents.** Every outcome an agent can produce has an explicit handler. The agent's work is fuzzy; the orchestration around it is not.\n66\t\n67\t---\n68\t\n69\t## 🧠 Core Principle\n70\t\n71\tNEEDLE is a **state machine**, not a script. Every bead transitions through a finite set of states, and every transition has a defined handler. There are no implicit fallbacks, no swallowed errors, no undefined paths.\n72\t\n73\t```\n74\tIf an outcome can happen, it has a handler.\n75\tIf it doesn't have a handler, it cannot happen.\n76\t```\n77\t\n78\t---\n79\t\n80\t## 🔄 The NEEDLE Algorithm\n81\t\n82\tA single worker executes this loop indefinitely:\n83\t\n84\t```\n85\t┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n86\t│                                                     │\n87\t│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\n88\t│   │  🔍 SELECT │◄────────────────────────────────┐  │\n89\t│   └─────┬─────┘                                  │  │\n90\t│         │                                        │  │\n91\t│         ▼                                        │  │\n92\t│   ┌───────────┐   race lost    ┌──────────┐     │  │\n93\t│   │  🔒 CLAIM  │──────────────►│ 🔁 RETRY  │─────┘  │\n94\t│   └─────┬─────┘               └──────────┘        │\n95\t│         │ claimed                                   │\n96\t│         ▼                                           │\n97\t│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\n98\t│   │ 📋 BUILD   │                                     │\n99\t│   └─────┬─────┘                                     │\n100\t│         │                                           │\n101\t│         ▼                                           │\n102\t│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\n103\t│   │ 🚀 DISPATCH│                                     │\n104\t│   └─────┬─────┘                                     │\n105\t│         │                                           │\n106\t│         ▼                                           │\n107\t│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\n108\t│   │ ⏳ EXECUTE │                                     │\n109\t│   └─────┬─────┘                                     │\n110\t│         │                                           │\n111\t│         ▼                                           │\n112\t│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\n113\t│   │ 📊 OUTCOME │                                     │\n114\t│   └─────┬─────┘                                     │\n115\t│         │                                           │\n116\t│         ├── ✅ success ──► close bead ──────────────┘\n117\t│         ├── ❌ failure ──► log + release ────────────┘\n118\t│         ├── ⏰ timeout ──► release + defer ──────────┘\n119\t│         └── 💀 crash ────► release + alert ──────────┘\n120\t│                                                     │\n121\t└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n122\t```\n123\t\n124\t---\n125\t\n126\t## 📐 Algorithm Steps\n127\t\n128\t### 🔍 Step 1: Select\n129\t\n130\tQuery the bead queue for the next claimable bead in **deterministic priority order**. Selection is not random — given the same queue state, every worker computes the same ordering. Ties are broken by creation time (oldest first).\n131\t\n132\t### 🔒 Step 2: Claim\n133\t\n134\tAttempt an **atomic claim** via `br update --claim`. SQLite transaction isolation guarantees exactly one worker succeeds. If the claim fails (race lost), return to Step 1 with the losing candidate excluded.\n135\t\n136\t### 📋 Step 3: Build\n137\t\n138\tConstruct the prompt from the bead's context: title, body, workspace path, relevant files, and any dependency context. The prompt is a deterministic function of the bead state — same bead, same prompt.\n139\t\n140\t### 🚀 Step 4: Dispatch\n141\t\n142\tLoad the agent adapter configuration (YAML), render the invoke template with the built prompt, and execute via `bash -c`. The agent runs headless — it receives a prompt, does work, and exits.\n143\t\n144\t### ⏳ Step 5: Execute\n145\t\n146\tThe agent runs. NEEDLE waits. The only inputs are the exit code and stdout/stderr. There is no interactive communication during execution.\n147\t\n148\t### 📊 Step 6: Outcome\n149\t\n150\tEvaluate the result and follow the **explicit path** for the observed outcome:\n151\t\n152\t| Outcome | Exit Code | Handler |\n153\t|---------|-----------|---------|\n154\t| ✅ **Success** | `0` | Validate output → close bead → log effort → **loop** |\n155\t| ❌ **Failure** | `1` | Log failure reason → release bead → increment retry count → **loop** |\n156\t| ⏰ **Timeout** | `124` | Release bead → mark deferred → **loop** |\n157\t| 💀 **Crash** | `>128` | Release bead → create alert bead → **loop** |\n158\t| 🏁 **Race Lost** | `4` | (Handled at Step 2) → exclude candidate → **retry select** |\n159\t| 🫙 **Queue Empty** | — | Enter strand escalation → **explore / mend / knot** |\n160\t\n161\tEvery row is implemented. There are no unhandled cases.\n162\t\n163\t---\n164\t\n165\t## 🧶 Strand Escalation\n166\t\n167\tWhen the primary workspace has no claimable beads, NEEDLE follows a **strand sequence** to find or create work. Each strand is evaluated in order — the first strand that yields a bead wins.\n168\t\n169\t| # | Strand | Agent? | Purpose |\n170\t|---|--------|--------|---------|\n171\t| 1 | 🪡 **Pluck** | Yes | Process beads from the assigned workspace |\n172\t| 2 | 🔧 **Mend** | No | Cleanup: orphaned claims, stale locks, health checks |\n173\t| 3 | 🔭 **Explore** | No | Search other workspaces for claimable beads |\n174\t| 4 | 🕸️ **Weave** | Yes | Create beads from documentation gaps *(opt-in)* |\n175\t| 5 | 🪢 **Unravel** | Yes | Propose alternatives for HUMAN-blocked beads *(opt-in)* |\n176\t| 6 | 💓 **Pulse** | Yes | Codebase health scans, auto-generate beads *(opt-in)* |\n177\t| 7 | 🪞 **Reflect** | Yes | Consolidate learnings from recent beads *(opt-in)* |\n178\t| 8 | 🪡 **Splice** | No | Document worker failures, create alert beads |\n179\t| 9 | 🪢 **Knot** | No | All strands exhausted — alert human, wait |\n180\t\n181\t---\n182\t\n183\t## ⚡ Parallel Workers\n184\t\n185\tMultiple NEEDLE workers run independently with **no central orchestrator**. Coordination happens through the shared bead queue:\n186\t\n187\t- **Atomicity** — `br update --claim` uses SQLite transactions; exactly one worker wins each claim\n188\t- **Determinism** — all workers compute the same priority order; races are resolved by the database, not by timing\n189\t- **Independence** — each worker is a self-contained loop in its own tmux session\n190\t- **Naming** — workers use NATO alphabet identifiers: `alpha`, `bravo`, `charlie`, ...\n191\t\n192\t```\n193\t  needle-claude-sonnet-alpha ──┐\n194\t  needle-claude-sonnet-bravo ──┤\n195\t  needle-codex-gpt4-charlie ───┼──► Shared .beads/ (SQLite + JSONL)\n196\t  needle-opencode-qwen-delta ──┤\n197\t  needle-aider-sonnet-echo ────┘\n198\t```\n199\t\n200\t---\n201\t\n202\t## 🏗️ Supported Agents\n203\t\n204\tNEEDLE is agent-agnostic. Any CLI that accepts a prompt and exits works.\n205\t\n206\t| Agent | CLI | Input Method | Notes |\n207\t|-------|-----|-------------|-------|\n208\t| Claude Code (interactive) | `claude-interactive` | stdin | **Recommended** — uses subscription billing; see [plugin](#-claude-interactive-plugin) |\n209\t| Claude Code (API) | `claude --print` | stdin | Uses programmatic/API billing |\n210\t| OpenCode | `opencode` | file | |\n211\t| Codex CLI | `codex` | args | |\n212\t| Aider | `aider --message` | args | |\n213\t| *Custom* | *any* | *configurable via YAML adapter* | |\n214\t\n215\tAdding a new agent requires **only a YAML configuration file** — no code changes.\n216\t\n217\t---\n218\t\n219\t## 🔌 claude-interactive Plugin\n220\t\n221\tThe `claude-interactive` plugin ships as a separate release asset. It wraps the Claude Code CLI in a PTY so workers run under your **Claude subscription** instead of consuming programmatic API credits.\n222\t\n223\t**How it works:** NEEDLE pipes subprocess stdio, which causes `claude` to detect a non-TTY and switch to API billing. `claude-interactive` creates an internal PTY so `claude` sees a real terminal, keeping it in interactive/subscription mode.\n224\t\n225\t**Install:**\n226\t\n227\t```bash\n228\t# Download the latest claude-interactive release\n229\tgh release download --repo jedarden/NEEDLE --pattern 'claude-interactive*'\n230\tchmod +x claude-interactive-install.sh\n231\t./claude-interactive-install.sh\n232\t```\n233\t\n234\t**Requirements:** Python 3.10+, `pyte` (`pip install pyte`), and the `claude` CLI on PATH.\n235\t\n236\t**Run:**\n237\t\n238\t```bash\n239\tcd /path/to/workspace\n240\tneedle run --agent claude-interactive --count 4\n241\t```\n242\t\n243\tSource lives in [`plugins/claude-interactive/`](plugins/claude-interactive/).\n244\t\n245\t---\n246\t\n247\t## 📁 Repository Structure\n248\t\n249\t```\n250\tNEEDLE/\n251\t├── Cargo.toml             # A silent worker is a broken worker.\n305\t\n306\t### Exported Signals\n307\t\n308\t| Signal | Description |\n309\t|--------|-------------|\n310\t| **Traces** | Spans for `worker.session`, `bead.lifecycle`, `bead.claim`, `agent.dispatch`, `strand.evaluated`, `outcome.handled` |\n311\t| **Metrics** | `needle.beads.completed`, `needle.beads.duration`, `needle.agent.tokens.input`, `needle.cost.usd`, and more |\n312\t| **Logs** | All events not represented as spans, with severity mapping (`ERROR` for failures, `WARN` for stale peers) |\n313\t\n314\t### OpenTelemetry (OTLP) Export\n315\t\n316\tNEEDLE can export telemetry to any OpenTelemetry-compatible backend (Jaeger, Tempo, Grafana, Honeycomb, Datadog, etc.) via OTLP.\n317\t\n318\t**Minimal configuration (`.needle.yaml`):**\n319\t\n320\t```yaml\n321\ttelemetry:\n322\t  otlp_sink:\n323\t    enabled: true\n324\t    endpoint: \"http://localhost:4317\"  # gRPC, or :4318 for HTTP\n325\t    protocol: \"grpc\"\n326\t```\n327\t\n328\t**Semantic conventions:** NEEDLE follows OpenTelemetry's `gen_ai.*` semantic conventions for LLM telemetry, enabling out-of-the-box integration with GenAI dashboards (Grafana GenAI app, Langfuse, Honeycomb AI, etc.).\n329\t\n330\tSee [`docs/plan/plan.md`](docs/plan/plan.md) for the complete semantic mapping table.\n331\t\n332\t---\n333\t\n334\t## 📊 Production Status\n335\t\n336\tNEEDLE currently powers my own headless multi-agent workflow — workers run continuously against shared bead queues, dispatching to Claude Code and other CLIs, with full OTLP telemetry wired through. Returns `None` (no match).\n248\t/// * Invalid glob pattern: Returns `None` (no match).\n249\t///\n250\t/// # Glob Pattern Syntax\n251\t///\n252\t/// * `*` - Matches any sequence of non-separator characters.\n253\t/// * `**` - Matches any sequence of characters, including path separators.\n254\t/// * `?` - Matches any single non-separator character.\n255\t/// * `[a-z]` - Matches any character in the bracket.\n256\t/// * `[!a-z]` - Matches any character not in the bracket.\n257\t///\n258\t/// # Examples\n259\t///\n260\t/// ```\n261\t/// use needle::routing::match_adapter_with_glob;\n262\t///\n263\t/// // Match with wildcard\n264\t/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-sonnet-4-6\").is_some());\n265\t/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-opus-4-6\").is_some());\n266\t/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"gpt-4\").is_none());\n267\t///\n268\t/// // Match with double wildcard\n269\t/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"**\", \"any-model\").is_some());\n270\t///\n271\t/// // Edge cases\n272\t/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"\", \"model\").is_none());\n273\t/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"pattern\", \"\").is_none());\n274\t/// ```\n275\tpub fn match_adapter_with_glob(pattern: &str, model_name: &str) -> Option<()> {\n276\t    // Handle edge cases\n277\t    if pattern.is_empty() || model_name.is_empty() {\n278\t        return None;\n279\t    }\n280\t\n281\t    // Use the glob crate to compile and match the pattern\n282\t    match glob::Pattern::new(pattern) {\n283\t        Ok(glob_pattern) => {\n284\t            // The glob crate's Pattern::matches takes a &str directly\n285\t            if glob_pattern.matches(model_name) {\n286\t                Some(())\n287\t            } else {\n288\t                None\n289\t            }\n290\t        }\n291\t        Err(_) => {\n292\t            // Invalid glob pattern\n293\t            None\n294\t        }\n295\t    }\n296\t}\n297\t\n298\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n299\t// Tests\n300\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n301\t\n302\t#[cfg(test)]\n303\tmod tests {\n304\t    use super::*;\n305\t    use crate::config::RoutingRule;\n306\t\n307\t    fn make_rule(pattern: &str, adapter: &str) -> RoutingRule {\n308\t        RoutingRule {\n309\t            match_model: pattern.to_string(),\n310\t            adapter: adapter.to_string(),\n311\t        }\n312\t    }\n313\t\n314\t    #[test]\n315\t    fn regex_pattern_match() {\n316\t        let rules = vec![make_rule(\"sonnet.*\",      }\n222\t\n223\t        // Explicit mapping for every exit code range — NO wildcards.\n224\t        // Each range is explicitly enumerated to ensure compile errors\n225\t        // if a new Outcome variant is added without updating this match.\n226\t        match exit_code {\n227\t            // Success\n228\t            0 => Outcome::Success,\n229\t            // Explicit failure code\n230\t            1 => Outcome::Failure,\n231\t            // Timeout (GNU timeout exit code)\n232\t            124 => Outcome::Timeout,\n233\t            // Agent not found (shell exit code for missing command)\n234\t            127 => Outcome::AgentNotFound,\n235\t            // Failure range: 2-123\n236\t            2..=123 => Outcome::Failure,\n237\t            // Failure: 125-128 (not >128 per spec, so 128 is not Crash)\n238\t            125..=128 => Outcome::Failure,\n239\t            // Signal exits: >128 (128 + signal number)\n240\t            // These are all crashes per the spec.\n241\t            129..=i32::MAX => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n242\t            // Negative exit codes (abnormal termination)\n243\t            i32::MIN..=-1 => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n244\t        }\n245\t    }\n246\t\n247\t    /// Return a string representation for telemetry/logging.\n248\t    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {\n249\t        match self {\n250\t            Outcome::Success => \"success\",\n251\t            Outcome::Failure => \"failure\",\n252\t            Outcome::Timeout => \"timeout\",\n253\t            Outcome::AgentNotFound => \"agent_not_found\",\n254\t            Outcome::Interrupted => \"interrupted\",\n255\t            Outcome::Crash(_) => \"crash\",\n256\t        }\n257\t    }\n258\t}\n259\t\n260\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n261\t// StrandError / StrandResult\n262\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n263\t\n264\t/// Error returned by a strand evaluation.\n265\t#[derive(Debug)]\n266\tpub enum StrandError {\n267\t    StoreError(anyhow::Error),\n268\t    ConfigError(String),\n269\t}\n270\t\n271\timpl fmt::Display for StrandError {\n272\t    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n273\t        match self {\n274\t            StrandError::StoreError(e) => write!(f, \"bead store error: {}\", e),\n275\t            StrandError::ConfigError(s) => write!(f, \"strand configuration error: {}\", s),\n276\t        }\n277\t    }\n278\t}\n279\t\n280\timpl std::error::Error for StrandError {\n281\t    fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)> {\n282\t        match self {\n283\t            StrandError::StoreError(e) => Some(e.as_ref()),\n284\t            StrandError::ConfigError(_) => None,\n285\t        }\n286\t    }\n287\t}\n288\t\n289\t/// Result of a strand 🧵 NEEDLE\\n4\\t\\n5\\t[![CI](https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/actions/workflows/ci.yml)\\n6\\t[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)\\n7\\t[![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/rust-1.75+-orange.svg)](rust-toolchain.toml)\\n8\\t[![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-0.2.8-green.svg)](Cargo.toml)\\n9\\t\\n10\\t**N**avigates **E**very **E**nqueued **D**eliverable, **L**ogs **E**ffort\\n11\\t\\n12\\t> Deterministic bead processing with explicit outcome paths.\\n13\\t\\n14\\tNEEDLE is a universal wrapper for headless coding CLI agents. It processes a shared bead queue in deterministic order, dispatching work to any headless CLI (Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Aider) and handling every outcome through an explicit, predefined path.\\n15\\t\\n16\\t---\\n17\\t\\n18\\t## 🚀 Quickstart\\n19\\t\\n20\\t```bash\\n21\\t# Install the latest release\\n22\\tcurl -fsSL https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash\\n23\\t\\n24\\t# Or build from source\\n25\\tcargo install --git https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE\\n26\\t\\n27\\t# Run a worker against a bead-tracked workspace\\n28\\tcd /path/to/your/workspace\\n29\\tneedle run --agent claude --identity alpha\\n30\\t```\\n31\\t\\n32\\tA worker starts, claims the next bead, dispatches to your chosen agent CLI, and loops. Multiple workers can run in parallel against the same workspace — coordination is handled by the shared bead queue (no central orchestrator).\\n33\\t\\n34\\tSee [`docs/examples/`](docs/examples/) for end-to-end configurations.\\n35\\t\\n36\\t---\\n37\\t\\n38\\t## 🧶 What is a bead?\\n39\\t\\n40\\tA **bead** is a work item — the unit of work NEEDLE processes. Think of it as a structured task ticket: a title, a body describing the deliverable and acceptance criteria, a status (`open`, `in_progress`, `done`), and optional metadata like priority and dependencies.\\n41\\t\\n42\\tBeads live in a **bead store** — a SQLite database (`beads.db`) plus a JSONL checkpoint file (`issues.jsonl`) in a `.beads/` directory inside your project. The `br` CLI manages the bead store: create beads, list them, claim them, close them.\\n43\\t\\n44\\t```bash\\n45\\t# Create a bead\\n46\\tbr create --title \\\"Add pagination to search results\\\" --body \\\"...\\\"\\n47\\t\\n48\\t# List open beads\\n49\\tbr list --status open\\n50\\t\\n51\\t# NEEDLE does the rest: claims, dispatches, and closes beads automatically\\n52\\t```\\n53\\t\\n54\\tNEEDLE workers read from this store, claim the next available bead atomically, dispatch it to your chosen agent CLI, and close it on success — then loop.\\n55\\t\\n56\\t---\\n57\\t\\n58\\t## 🤔 Why NEEDLE\\n59\\t\\n60\\tExisting agent orchestration tools are built for one of two shapes:\\n61\\t\\n62\\t- **Conversational frameworks** (LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI) assume a chat loop with a human-in-the-loop or another LLM. They are bad at headless, long-running, cost-bounded work.\\n63\\t- **Workflow engines** (Temporal, Argo Workflows, Inngest) assume each step is deterministic code. They are bad at non-deterministic agent steps whose outcomes have to be classified and routed.\\n64\\t\\n65\\tNEEDLE is the missing middle: a **deterministic state machine that drives non-deterministic agents.** Every outcome an agent can produce has an explicit handler. The agent's work is fuzzy; the orchestration around it is not.\\n66\\t\\n67\\t---\\n68\\t\\n69\\t## 🧠 Core Principle\\n70\\t\\n71\\tNEEDLE is a **state machine**, not a script. Every bead transitions through a finite set of states, and every transition has a defined handler. There are no implicit fallbacks, no swallowed errors, no undefined paths.\\n72\\t\\n73\\t```\\n74\\tIf an outcome can happen, it has a handler.\\n75\\tIf it doesn't have a handler, it cannot happen.\\n76\\t```\\n77\\t\\n78\\t---\\n79\\t\\n80\\t## 🔄 The NEEDLE Algorithm\\n81\\t\\n82\\tA single worker executes this loop indefinitely:\\n83\\t\\n84\\t```\\n85\\t┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\\n86\\t│                                                     │\\n87\\t│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\\n88\\t│   │  🔍 SELECT │◄────────────────────────────────┐  │\\n89\\t│   └─────┬─────┘                                  │  │\\n90\\t│         │                                        │  │\\n91\\t│         ▼                                        │  │\\n92\\t│   ┌───────────┐   race lost    ┌──────────┐     │  │\\n93\\t│   │  🔒 CLAIM  │──────────────►│ 🔁 RETRY  │─────┘  │\\n94\\t│   └─────┬─────┘               └──────────┘        │\\n95\\t│         │ claimed                                   │\\n96\\t│         ▼                                           │\\n97\\t│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\\n98\\t│   │ 📋 BUILD   │                                     │\\n99\\t│   └─────┬─────┘                                     │\\n100\\t│         │                                           │\\n101\\t│         ▼                                           │\\n102\\t│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\\n103\\t│   │ 🚀 DISPATCH│                                     │\\n104\\t│   └─────┬─────┘                                     │\\n105\\t│         │                                           │\\n106\\t│         ▼                                           │\\n107\\t│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\\n108\\t│   │ ⏳ EXECUTE │                                     │\\n109\\t│   └─────┬─────┘                                     │\\n110\\t│         │                                           │\\n111\\t│         ▼                                           │\\n112\\t│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\\n113\\t│   │ 📊 OUTCOME │                                     │\\n114\\t│   └─────┬─────┘                                     │\\n115\\t│         │                                           │\\n116\\t│         ├── ✅ success ──► close bead ──────────────┘\\n117\\t│         ├── ❌ failure ──► log + release ────────────┘\\n118\\t│         ├── ⏰ timeout ──► release + defer ──────────┘\\n119\\t│         └── 💀 crash ────► release + alert ──────────┘\\n120\\t│                                                     │\\n121\\t└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\\n122\\t```\\n123\\t\\n124\\t---\\n125\\t\\n126\\t## 📐 Algorithm Steps\\n127\\t\\n128\\t### 🔍 Step 1: Select\\n129\\t\\n130\\tQuery the bead queue for the next claimable bead in **deterministic priority order**. Selection is not random — given the same queue state, every worker computes the same ordering. Ties are broken by creation time (oldest first).\\n131\\t\\n132\\t### 🔒 Step 2: Claim\\n133\\t\\n134\\tAttempt an **atomic claim** via `br update --claim`. SQLite transaction isolation guarantees exactly one worker succeeds. If the claim fails (race lost), return to Step 1 with the losing candidate excluded.\\n135\\t\\n136\\t### 📋 Step 3: Build\\n137\\t\\n138\\tConstruct the prompt from the bead's context: title, body, workspace path, relevant files, and any dependency context. The prompt is a deterministic function of the bead state — same bead, same prompt.\\n139\\t\\n140\\t### 🚀 Step 4: Dispatch\\n141\\t\\n142\\tLoad the agent adapter configuration (YAML), render the invoke template with the built prompt, and execute via `bash -c`. The agent runs headless — it receives a prompt, does work, and exits.\\n143\\t\\n144\\t### ⏳ Step 5: Execute\\n145\\t\\n146\\tThe agent runs. NEEDLE waits. The only inputs are the exit code and stdout/stderr. There is no interactive communication during execution.\\n147\\t\\n148\\t### 📊 Step 6: Outcome\\n149\\t\\n150\\tEvaluate the result and follow the **explicit path** for the observed outcome:\\n151\\t\\n152\\t| Outcome | Exit Code | Handler |\\n153\\t|---------|-----------|---------|\\n154\\t| ✅ **Success** | `0` | Validate output → close bead → log effort → **loop** |\\n155\\t| ❌ **Failure** | `1` | Log failure reason → release bead → increment retry count → **loop** |\\n156\\t| ⏰ **Timeout** | `124` | Release bead → mark deferred → **loop** |\\n157\\t| 💀 **Crash** | `>128` | Release bead → create alert bead → **loop** |\\n158\\t| 🏁 **Race Lost** | `4` | (Handled at Step 2) → exclude candidate → **retry select** |\\n159\\t| 🫙 **Queue Empty** | — | Enter strand escalation → **explore / mend / knot** |\\n160\\t\\n161\\tEvery row is implemented. There are no unhandled cases.\\n162\\t\\n163\\t---\\n164\\t\\n165\\t## 🧶 Strand Escalation\\n166\\t\\n167\\tWhen the primary workspace has no claimable beads, NEEDLE follows a **strand sequence** to find or create work. Each strand is evaluated in order — the first strand that yields a bead wins.\\n168\\t\\n169\\t| # | Strand | Agent? | Purpose |\\n170\\t|---|--------|--------|---------|\\n171\\t| 1 | 🪡 **Pluck** | Yes | Process beads from the assigned workspace |\\n172\\t| 2 | 🔧 **Mend** | No | Cleanup: orphaned claims, stale locks, health checks |\\n173\\t| 3 | 🔭 **Explore** | No | Search other workspaces for claimable beads |\\n174\\t| 4 | 🕸️ **Weave** | Yes | Create beads from documentation gaps *(opt-in)* |\\n175\\t| 5 | 🪢 **Unravel** | Yes | Propose alternatives for HUMAN-blocked beads *(opt-in)* |\\n176\\t| 6 | 💓 **Pulse** | Yes | Codebase health scans, auto-generate beads *(opt-in)* |\\n177\\t| 7 | 🪞 **Reflect** | Yes | Consolidate learnings from recent beads *(opt-in)* |\\n178\\t| 8 | 🪡 **Splice** | No | Document worker failures, create alert beads |\\n179\\t| 9 | 🪢 **Knot** | No | All strands exhausted — alert human, wait |\\n180\\t\\n181\\t---\\n182\\t\\n183\\t## ⚡ Parallel Workers\\n184\\t\\n185\\tMultiple NEEDLE workers run independently with **no central orchestrator**. Coordination happens through the shared bead queue:\\n186\\t\\n187\\t- **Atomicity** — `br update --claim` uses SQLite transactions; exactly one worker wins each claim\\n188\\t- **Determinism** — all workers compute the same priority order; races are resolved by the database, not by timing\\n189\\t- **Independence** — each worker is a self-contained loop in its own tmux session\\n190\\t- **Naming** — workers use NATO alphabet identifiers: `alpha`, `bravo`, `charlie`, ...\\n191\\t\\n192\\t```\\n193\\t  needle-claude-sonnet-alpha ──┐\\n194\\t  needle-claude-sonnet-bravo ──┤\\n195\\t  needle-codex-gpt4-charlie ───┼──► Shared .beads/ (SQLite + JSONL)\\n196\\t  needle-opencode-qwen-delta ──┤\\n197\\t  needle-aider-sonnet-echo ────┘\\n198\\t```\\n199\\t\\n200\\t---\\n201\\t\\n202\\t## 🏗️ Supported Agents\\n203\\t\\n204\\tNEEDLE is agent-agnostic. Any CLI that accepts a prompt and exits works.\\n205\\t\\n206\\t| Agent | CLI | Input Method | Notes |\\n207\\t|-------|-----|-------------|-------|\\n208\\t| Claude Code (interactive) | `claude-interactive` | stdin | **Recommended** — uses subscription billing; see [plugin](#-claude-interactive-plugin) |\\n209\\t| Claude Code (API) | `claude --print` | stdin | Uses programmatic/API billing |\\n210\\t| OpenCode | `opencode` | file | |\\n211\\t| Codex CLI | `codex` | args | |\\n212\\t| Aider | `aider --message` | args | |\\n213\\t| *Custom* | *any* | *configurable via YAML adapter* | |\\n214\\t\\n215\\tAdding a new agent requires **only a YAML configuration file** — no code changes.\\n216\\t\\n217\\t---\\n218\\t\\n219\\t## 🔌 claude-interactive Plugin\\n220\\t\\n221\\tThe `claude-interactive` plugin ships as a separate release asset. `Some(())` - The pattern matches the model name.\\n242\\t/// * `None` - The pattern does not match or is invalid.\\n243\\t///\\n244\\t/// # Edge Cases\\n245\\t///\\n246\\t/// * Empty pattern: Returns `None` (no match).\\n247\\t/// * Empty model name: Returns `None` (no match).\\n248\\t/// * Invalid glob pattern: Returns `None` (no match).\\n249\\t///\\n250\\t/// # Glob Pattern Syntax\\n251\\t///\\n252\\t/// * `*` - Matches any sequence of non-separator characters.\\n253\\t/// * `**` - Matches any sequence of characters, including path separators.\\n254\\t/// * `?` - Matches any single non-separator character.\\n255\\t/// * `[a-z]` - Matches any character in the bracket.\\n256\\t/// * `[!a-z]` - Matches any character not in the bracket.\\n257\\t///\\n258\\t/// # Examples\\n259\\t///\\n260\\t/// ```\\n261\\t/// use needle::routing::match_adapter_with_glob;\\n262\\t///\\n263\\t/// // Match with wildcard\\n264\\t/// {\\n292\\t            // Invalid glob pattern\\n293\\t            None\\n294\\t        }\\n295\\t    }\\n296\\t}\\n297\\t\\n298\\t// 🧵 NEEDLE\\n4\\t\\n5\\t[![CI](https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/actions/workflows/ci.yml)\\n6\\t[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)\\n7\\t[![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/rust-1.75+-orange.svg)](rust-toolchain.toml)\\n8\\t[![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-0.2.8-green.svg)](Cargo.toml)\\n9\\t\\n10\\t**N**avigates **E**very **E**nqueued **D**eliverable, **L**ogs **E**ffort\\n11\\t\\n12\\t> Deterministic bead processing with explicit outcome paths.\\n13\\t\\n14\\tNEEDLE is a universal wrapper for headless coding CLI agents. It processes a shared bead queue in deterministic order, dispatching work to any headless CLI (Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Aider) and handling every outcome through an explicit, predefined path.\\n15\\t\\n16\\t---\\n17\\t\\n18\\t## 🚀 Quickstart\\n19\\t\\n20\\t```bash\\n21\\t# Install the latest release\\n22\\tcurl -fsSL https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash\\n23\\t\\n24\\t# Or build from source\\n25\\tcargo install --git https://github.com/jedarden/NEEDLE\\n26\\t\\n27\\t# Run a worker against a bead-tracked workspace\\n28\\tcd /path/to/your/workspace\\n29\\tneedle run --agent claude --identity alpha\\n30\\t```\\n31\\t\\n32\\tA worker starts, claims the next bead, dispatches to your chosen agent CLI, and loops. Multiple workers can run in parallel against the same workspace — coordination is handled by the shared bead queue (no central orchestrator).\\n33\\t\\n34\\tSee [`docs/examples/`](docs/examples/) for end-to-end configurations.\\n35\\t\\n36\\t---\\n37\\t\\n38\\t## 🧶 What is a bead?\\n39\\t\\n40\\tA **bead** is a work item — the unit of work NEEDLE processes. Think of it as a structured task ticket: a title, a body describing the deliverable and acceptance criteria, a status (`open`, `in_progress`, `done`), and optional metadata like priority and dependencies.\\n41\\t\\n42\\tBeads live in a **bead store** — a SQLite database (`beads.db`) plus a JSONL checkpoint file (`issues.jsonl`) in a `.beads/` directory inside your project. The `br` CLI manages the bead store: create beads, list them, claim them, close them.\\n43\\t\\n44\\t```bash\\n45\\t# Create a bead\\n46\\tbr create --title \\\"Add pagination to search results\\\" --body \\\"...\\\"\\n47\\t\\n48\\t# List open beads\\n49\\tbr list --status open\\n50\\t\\n51\\t# NEEDLE does the rest: claims, dispatches, and closes beads automatically\\n52\\t```\\n53\\t\\n54\\tNEEDLE workers read from this store, claim the next available bead atomically, dispatch it to your chosen agent CLI, and close it on success — then loop.\\n55\\t\\n56\\t---\\n57\\t\\n58\\t## 🤔 Why NEEDLE\\n59\\t\\n60\\tExisting agent orchestration tools are built for one of two shapes:\\n61\\t\\n62\\t- **Conversational frameworks** (LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI) assume a chat loop with a human-in-the-loop or another LLM. They are bad at headless, long-running, cost-bounded work.\\n63\\t- **Workflow engines** (Temporal, Argo Workflows, Inngest) assume each step is deterministic code. They are bad at non-deterministic agent steps whose outcomes have to be classified and routed.\\n64\\t\\n65\\tNEEDLE is the missing middle: a **deterministic state machine that drives non-deterministic agents.** Every outcome an agent can produce has an explicit handler. The agent's work is fuzzy; the orchestration around it is not.\\n66\\t\\n67\\t---\\n68\\t\\n69\\t## 🧠 Core Principle\\n70\\t\\n71\\tNEEDLE is a **state machine**, not a script. Every bead transitions through a finite set of states, and every transition has a defined handler. There are no implicit fallbacks, no swallowed errors, no undefined paths.\\n72\\t\\n73\\t```\\n74\\tIf an outcome can happen, it has a handler.\\n75\\tIf it doesn't have a handler, it cannot happen.\\n76\\t```\\n77\\t\\n78\\t---\\n79\\t\\n80\\t## 🔄 The NEEDLE Algorithm\\n81\\t\\n82\\tA single worker executes this loop indefinitely:\\n83\\t\\n84\\t```\\n85\\t┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\\n86\\t│                                                     │\\n87\\t│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\\n88\\t│   │  🔍 SELECT │◄────────────────────────────────┐  │\\n89\\t│   └─────┬─────┘                                  │  │\\n90\\t│         │                                        │  │\\n91\\t│         ▼                                        │  │\\n92\\t│   ┌───────────┐   race lost    ┌──────────┐     │  │\\n93\\t│   │  🔒 CLAIM  │──────────────►│ 🔁 RETRY  │─────┘  │\\n94\\t│   └─────┬─────┘               └──────────┘        │\\n95\\t│         │ claimed                                   │\\n96\\t│         ▼                                           │\\n97\\t│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\\n98\\t│   │ 📋 BUILD   │                                     │\\n99\\t│   └─────┬─────┘                                     │\\n100\\t│         │                                           │\\n101\\t│         ▼                                           │\\n102\\t│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\\n103\\t│   │ 🚀 DISPATCH│                                     │\\n104\\t│   └─────┬─────┘                                     │\\n105\\t│         │                                           │\\n106\\t│         ▼                                           │\\n107\\t│   ┌───────────┐                                     │\\n108\\t│   │ ⏳ EXECUTE │                                     │\\n109\\t│   └─────┬─────┘                                     │\\n110\\t│         │                                           │\\n111\\t│         ▼                                           │\\n112\\t│   ┌───────────┐ │\\n121\\t└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\\n122\\t```\\n123\\t\\n124\\t---\\n125\\t\\n126\\t## 📐 Algorithm Steps\\n127\\t\\n128\\t### 🔍 Step 1: Select\\n129\\t\\n130\\tQuery the bead queue for the next claimable bead in **deterministic priority order**. Selection is not random — given the same queue state, every worker computes the same ordering. Ties are broken by creation time (oldest first).\\n131\\t\\n132\\t### 🔒 Step 2: Claim\\n133\\t\\n134\\tAttempt an **atomic claim** via `br update --claim`. SQLite transaction isolation guarantees exactly one worker succeeds. If the claim fails (race lost), return to Step 1 with the losing candidate excluded.\\n135\\t\\n136\\t### 📋 Step 3: Build\\n137\\t\\n138\\tConstruct the prompt from the bead's context: title, body, workspace path, relevant files, and any dependency context. The prompt is a deterministic function of the bead state — same bead, same prompt.\\n139\\t\\n140\\t### 🚀 Step 4: Dispatch\\n141\\t\\n142\\tLoad the agent adapter configuration (YAML), render the invoke template with the built prompt, and execute via `bash -c`. The agent runs headless — it receives a prompt, does work, and exits.\\n143\\t\\n144\\t### ⏳ Step 5: Execute\\n145\\t\\n146\\tThe agent runs. NEEDLE waits. The only inputs are the exit code and stdout/stderr. There is no interactive communication during execution.\\n147\\t\\n148\\t### 📊 Step 6: Outcome\\n149\\t\\n150\\tEvaluate the result and follow the **explicit path** for the observed outcome:\\n151\\t\\n152\\t| Outcome | Exit Code | Handler |\\n153\\t|---------|-----------|---------|\\n154\\t| ✅ **Success** | `0` | Validate output → close bead → log effort → **loop** |\\n155\\t| ❌ **Failure** | `1` | Log failure reason → release bead → increment retry count → **loop** |\\n156\\t| ⏰ **Timeout** | `124` | Release bead → mark deferred → **loop** |\\n157\\t| 💀 **Crash** | `>128` | Release bead → create alert bead → **loop** |\\n158\\t| 🏁 **Race Lost** | `4` | (Handled at Step 2) → exclude candidate → **retry select** |\\n159\\t| 🫙 **Queue Empty** | — | Enter strand escalation → **explore / mend / knot** |\\n160\\t\\n161\\tEvery row is implemented. There are no unhandled cases.\\n162\\t\\n163\\t---\\n164\\t\\n165\\t## 🧶 Strand Escalation\\n166\\t\\n167\\tWhen the primary workspace has no claimable beads, NEEDLE follows a **strand sequence** to find or create work. Each strand is evaluated in order — the first strand that yields a bead wins.\\n168\\t\\n169\\t| # | Strand | Agent? | Purpose |\\n170\\t|---|--------|--------|---------|\\n171\\t| 1 | 🪡 **Pluck** | Yes | Process beads from the assigned workspace |\\n172\\t| 2 | 🔧 **Mend** | No | Cleanup: orphaned claims, stale locks, health checks |\\n173\\t| 3 | 🔭 **Explore** | No | Search other workspaces for claimable beads |\\n174\\t| 4 | 🕸️ **Weave** | Yes | Create beads from documentation gaps *(opt-in)* |\\n175\\t| 5 | 🪢 **Unravel** | Yes | Propose alternatives for HUMAN-blocked beads *(opt-in)* |\\n176\\t| 6 | 💓 **Pulse** | Yes | Codebase health scans, auto-generate beads *(opt-in)* |\\n177\\t| 7 | 🪞 **Reflect** | Yes | Consolidate learnings from recent beads *(opt-in)* |\\n178\\t| 8 | 🪡 **Splice** | No | Document worker failures, create alert beads |\\n179\\t| 9 | 🪢 **Knot** | No | All strands exhausted — alert human, wait |\\n180\\t\\n181\\t---\\n182\\t\\n183\\t## ⚡ Parallel Workers\\n184\\t\\n185\\tMultiple NEEDLE workers run independently with **no central orchestrator**. Coordination happens through the shared bead queue:\\n186\\t\\n187\\t- **Atomicity** — `br update --claim` uses SQLite transactions; exactly one worker wins each claim\\n188\\t- **Determinism** — all workers compute the same priority order; races are resolved by the database, not by timing\\n189\\t- **Independence** — each worker is a self-contained loop in its own tmux session\\n190\\t- **Naming** — workers use NATO alphabet identifiers: `alpha`, `bravo`, `charlie`, ...\\n191\\t\\n192\\t```\\n193\\t  needle-claude-sonnet-alpha ──┐\\n194\\t  needle-claude-sonnet-bravo ──┤\\n195\\t  needle-codex-gpt4-charlie ───┼──► Shared .beads/ (SQLite + JSONL)\\n196\\t  needle-opencode-qwen-delta ──┤\\n197\\t  needle-aider-sonnet-echo ────┘\\n198\\t```\\n199\\t\\n200\\t---\\n201\\t\\n202\\t## 🏗️ Supported Agents\\n203\\t\\n204\\tNEEDLE is agent-agnostic. Any CLI that accepts a prompt and exits works.\\n205\\t\\n206\\t| Agent | CLI | Input Method | Notes |\\n207\\t|-------|-----|-------------|-------|\\n208\\t| Claude Code (interactive) | `claude-interactive` | stdin | **Recommended** — uses subscription billing; see [plugin](#-claude-interactive-plugin) |\\n209\\t| Claude Code (API) | `claude --print` | stdin | Uses programmatic/API billing |\\n210\\t| OpenCode | `opencode` | file | |\\n211\\t| Codex CLI | `codex` | args | |\\n212\\t| Aider | `aider --message` | args | |\\n213\\t| *Custom* | *any* | *configurable via YAML adapter* | |\\n214\\t\\n215\\tAdding a new agent requires **only a YAML configuration file** — no code changes.\\n216\\t\\n217\\t---\\n218\\t\\n219\\t## 🔌 claude-interactive Plugin\\n220\\t\\n221\\tThe `claude-interactive` plugin ships as a separate release asset. Escaped `\\\\*` and `\\\\*\\\\*` treated literally\\n103\\t/// - No implicit start anchor for glob patterns (unlike regex patterns)\\n104\\tfn convert_glob_to_regex(glob: &str) -> String {\\n105\\t    // Special case: * and ** should match anything (including empty).\\n106\\t    if glob == \\\"*\\\" || glob == \\\"**\\\" {\\n107\\t        return \\\"^.*$\\\".to_string();\\n108\\t    }\\n109\\t\\n110\\t    let mut result = String::new();\\n111\\t    let chars: Vec<char> = glob.chars().collect();\\n112\\t    let mut i = 0;\\n113\\t\\n114\\t    while i < chars.len() {\\n115\\t        match chars[i] {\\n116\\t            '\\\\\\\\' => {\\n117\\t                // Escaped character - pass through the backslash and the character.\\n118\\t                // This ensures that \\\\* in the glob becomes \\\\* in the regex (literal asterisk).\\n119\\t                if i + 1 < chars.len() {\\n120\\t                    result.push('\\\\\\\\');\\n121\\t                    result.push(chars[i + 1]);\\n122\\t                    i += 2;\\n123\\t                } else {\\n124\\t                    // Trailing backslash - treat literally.\\n125\\t                    result.push('\\\\\\\\');\\n126\\t                    i += 1;\\n127\\t                }\\n128\\t            }\\n129\\t            '*' => {\\n130\\t                // Check for **.\\n131\\t                if i + 1 < chars.len() && chars[i + 1] == '*' {\\n132\\t                    // ** matches any characters including slashes.\\n133\\t                    result.push_str(\\\".*\\\");\\n134\\t                    i += 2;\\n135\\t                } else {\\n136\\t                    // * matches any non-slash characters.\\n137\\t                    result.push_str(\\\"[^/]+\\\");\\n138\\t                    i += 1;\\n139\\t                }\\n140\\t            }\\n141\\t            c => {\\n142\\t                // Pass through regex metacharacters literally - regex::Regex::new\\n143\\t                // will handle escaping. We only need to escape backslashes for\\n144\\t                // the glob conversion.\\n145\\t                result.push(c);\\n146\\t                i += 1;\\n147\\t            }\\n148\\t        }\\n149\\t    }\\n150\\t\\n151\\t    // Only add end anchor, not start anchor (glob patterns match substrings).\\n152\\t    format!(\\\"{}$\\\", result)\\n153\\t}\\n154\\t\\n155\\t/// Match a model name against routing rules, returning the adapter to use.\\n156\\t///\\n157\\t/// Evaluates rules in order; the first matching rule determines the adapter.\\n158\\t/// If no rule matches, returns the default adapter.\\n159\\t///\\n160\\t/// # Arguments\\n161\\t///\\n162\\t/// * `model` - The model name to match (e.g., \\\"claude-sonnet-4-6\\\").\\n163\\t/// * `rules` - Ordered list of routing rules (first match wins).\\n164\\t/// * `default` - Fallback adapter when no rules match.\\n165\\t///\\n166\\t/// # Returns\\n167\\t///\\n168\\t/// * `Some(adapter)` - The adapter name to use.\\n169\\t/// * `None` - No rule matched and default is empty/invalid (caller should handle).\\n170\\t///\\n171\\t/// # Examples\\n172\\t///\\n173\\t/// ```\\n174\\t/// use );\\n199\\t/// ```\\n200\\tpub fn match_adapter(model: &str, rules: &[RoutingRule], default: &str) -> Option<String> {\\n201\\t    // Compile rules and test in order (first match wins).\\n202\\t    for rule in rules {\\n203\\t        match CompiledRule::from_rule(rule) {\\n204\\t            Ok(compiled) => {\\n205\\t                if compiled.matches(model) {\\n206\\t                    return Some(compiled.adapter.clone());\\n207\\t                }\\n208\\t            }\\n209\\t            Err(e) => {\\n210\\t                // Log the error but continue with other rules.\\n211\\t rule matched — use default if provided.\\n222\\t    if default.is_empty() {\\n223\\t        None\\n224\\t    } else {\\n225\\t        Some(default.to_string())\\n226\\t    }\\n227\\t}\\n228\\t\\n229\\t/// Match a model name against a single glob pattern using the glob crate.\\n230\\t///\\n231\\t/// This is a lower-level function that tests if a glob pattern matches a model name.\\n232\\t/// It uses the `glob` crate's Pattern type directly for glob-style pattern matching.\\n233\\t///\\n234\\t/// # Arguments\\n235\\t///\\n236\\t/// * `pattern` - Glob pattern to `Some(())` - The pattern matches the model name.\\n242\\t/// * `None` - The pattern does not match or is invalid.\\n243\\t///\\n244\\t/// # Edge Cases\\n245\\t///\\n246\\t/// * Empty pattern: Returns `None` (no match).\\n247\\t/// * Empty model name: Returns `None` (no match).\\n248\\t/// * Invalid glob pattern: Returns `None` (no match).\\n249\\t///\\n250\\t/// # Glob Pattern Syntax\\n251\\t///\\n252\\t/// * `*` - Matches any sequence of non-separator characters.\\n253\\t/// * `**` - Matches any sequence of characters, including path separators.\\n254\\t/// * `?` - Matches Routing rule matcher for model-to-adapter dispatch.\n//!\n//! Provides pattern matching logic for routing rules: regex/glob patterns\n//! against model names, first-match-wins semantics, and default fallback.\n\nuse crate::config::RoutingRule;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\n/// Compiled routing rule with cached regex for efficient matching.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\nstruct CompiledRule {\n    /// Compiled regex matcher.\n    matcher: Arc<regex::Regex>,\n    /// Adapter to use on match.\n    adapter: String,\n}\n\nimpl CompiledRule {\n    /// Compile a routing rule into an efficient matcher.\n    ///\n    /// Supports both regex patterns (any valid regex) and glob-style patterns:\n    /// - `*` matches any single path segment (non-greedy `[^/]+`)\n    /// - `**` matches zero or more path segments (`.+?` with greedy quantifier)\n    /// - Literal `*` or `**` must be escaped as `\\*` or `\\*\\*`\n    fn from_rule(rule: &RoutingRule) -> Result<Self, regex::Error> {\n        let pattern = &rule.match_model;\n        let adapter = rule.adapter.clone();\n\n        // Convert glob patterns to regex if needed.\n        // If the pattern contains * or ** without proper regex escaping,\n        // treat it as a glob pattern and convert.\n        let regex_pattern = if needs_glob_conversion(pattern) {\n            convert_glob_to_regex(pattern)\n        } else {\n            pattern.clone()\n        };\n\n        let matcher = regex::Regex::new(&regex_pattern)?;\n\n        Ok(CompiledRule {\n            matcher: Arc::new(matcher),\n            adapter,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Test if a model name matches this rule.\n    fn matches(&self, model: &str) -> bool {\n        self.matcher.is_match(model)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Check if a pattern contains glob-style wildcards that need conversion.\n///\n/// Returns true if the pattern appears to be a glob pattern rather than\n/// a well-formed regex. The heuristic checks for:\n/// 1. Regex features: anchors (^$), character classes [], parentheses (),\n///    quantifiers +?{}, alternation |, or the regex wildcard sequence .*\n/// 2. If present, it's a regex pattern - no conversion needed\n/// 3. If absent, but * is present, it's a glob pattern - convert it\nfn needs_glob_conversion(pattern: &str) -> bool {\n    // First, check if it looks like a regex by looking for regex metacharacters.\n    // The key indicator is .* which is \"any character\" in regex but not in glob.\n    let has_regex_features = pattern.contains(|c| {\n        matches!(\n            c,\n            '^' | '$' | '(' | ')' | '[' | ']' | '{' | '}' | '+' | '?' | '|' | '\\\\'\n        )\n    }) || pattern.contains(\".*\");\n\n    if has_regex_features {\n        // Has clear regex features - treat as regex\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    // At this point, we have a simple pattern that might be glob or regex.\n    // If it contains unescaped * (and we already ruled out other regex chars),\n    // treat it as a glob pattern.\n    let chars: Vec<char> = pattern.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        if chars[i] == '\\\\' && i + 1 < chars.len() {\n            // Skip escaped character.\n            i += 2;\n            continue;\n        }\n        if chars[i] == '*' {\n            return true;\n        }\n        i += 1;\n    }\n\n    false\n}\n\n/// Convert glob-style pattern to regex.\n///\n/// Rules:\n/// - `*` alone → `.*` (match anything, catch-all)\n/// - `*` in other contexts → `[^/]+` (match any single segment, no slashes)\n/// - `**` → `.*` (match any characters including slashes, greedy)\n/// - Escaped `\\*` and `\\*\\*` treated literally\n/// - No implicit start anchor for glob patterns (unlike regex patterns)\nfn convert_glob_to_regex(glob: &str) -> String {\n    // Special case: * and ** should match anything (including empty).\n    if glob == \"*\" || glob == \"**\" {\n        return \"^.*$\".to_string();\n    }\n\n    let mut result = String::new();\n    let chars: Vec<char> = glob.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        match chars[i] {\n            '\\\\' => {\n                // Escaped character - pass through the backslash and the character.\n                // This ensures that \\* in the glob becomes \\* in the regex (literal asterisk).\n                if i + 1 < chars.len() {\n                    result.push('\\\\');\n                    result.push(chars[i + 1]);\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    // Trailing backslash - treat literally.\n                    result.push('\\\\');\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            '*' => {\n                // Check for **.\n                if i + 1 < chars.len() && chars[i + 1] == '*' {\n                    // ** matches any characters including slashes.\n                    result.push_str(\".*\");\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    // * matches any non-slash characters.\n                    result.push_str(\"[^/]+\");\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            c => {\n                // Pass through regex metacharacters literally - regex::Regex::new\n                // will handle escaping. We only need to escape backslashes for\n                // the glob conversion.\n                result.push(c);\n                i += 1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Only add end anchor, not start anchor (glob patterns match substrings).\n    format!(\"{}$\", result)\n}\n\n/// Match a model name against routing rules, returning the adapter to use.\n///\n/// Evaluates rules in order; the first matching rule determines the adapter.\n/// If no rule matches, returns the default adapter.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `model` - The model name to match (e.g., \"claude-sonnet-4-6\").\n/// * `rules` - Ordered list of routing rules (first match wins).\n/// * `default` - Fallback adapter when no rules match.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Some(adapter)` - The adapter name to use.\n/// * `None` - No rule matched and default is empty/invalid (caller should handle).\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::routing::match_adapter;\n/// use needle::config::RoutingRule;\n///\n/// let rules = vec![\n///     RoutingRule {\n///         match_model: \"sonnet.*\".to_string(),\n///         adapter: \"claude-print\".to_string(),\n///     },\n///     RoutingRule {\n///         match_model: \"*\".to_string(),\n///         adapter: \"default-adapter\".to_string(),\n///     },\n/// ];\n///\n/// // First rule matches.\n/// assert_eq!(\n///     match_adapter(\"sonnet-4-6\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n///     Some(\"claude-print\".to_string())\n/// );\n///\n/// // Second rule (catch-all) matches.\n/// assert_eq!(\n///     match_adapter(\"other-model\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n///     Some(\"default-adapter\".to_string())\n/// );\n/// ```\npub fn match_adapter(model: &str, rules: &[RoutingRule], default: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    // Compile rules and test in order (first match wins).\n    for rule in rules {\n        match CompiledRule::from_rule(rule) {\n            Ok(compiled) => {\n                if compiled.matches(model) {\n                    return Some(compiled.adapter.clone());\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                // Log the error but continue with other rules.\n                // Invalid patterns are skipped rather than failing the entire dispatch.\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    pattern = %rule.match_model,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"invalid routing pattern — skipping rule\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // No rule matched — use default if provided.\n    if default.is_empty() {\n        None\n    } else {\n        Some(default.to_string())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Match a model name against a single glob pattern using the glob crate.\n///\n/// This is a lower-level function that tests if a glob pattern matches a model name.\n/// It uses the `glob` crate's Pattern type directly for glob-style pattern matching.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `pattern` - Glob pattern to match (e.g., \"claude-*\", \"gpt-*\", \"*\").\n/// * `model_name` - The model name to test against the pattern.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Some(())` - The pattern matches the model name.\n/// * `None` - The pattern does not match or is invalid.\n///\n/// # Edge Cases\n///\n/// * Empty pattern: Returns `None` (no match).\n/// * Empty model name: Returns `None` (no match).\n/// * Invalid glob pattern: Returns `None` (no match).\n///\n/// # Glob Pattern Syntax\n///\n/// * `*` - Matches any sequence of non-separator characters.\n/// * `**` - Matches any sequence of characters, including path separators.\n/// * `?` - Matches any single non-separator character.\n/// * `[a-z]` - Matches any character in the bracket.\n/// * `[!a-z]` - Matches any character not in the bracket.\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::routing::match_adapter_with_glob;\n///\n/// // Match with wildcard\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-sonnet-4-6\").is_some());\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-opus-4-6\").is_some());\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"gpt-4\").is_none());\n///\n/// // Match with double wildcard\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"**\", \"any-model\").is_some());\n///\n/// // Edge cases\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"\", \"model\").is_none());\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"pattern\", \"\").is_none());\n/// ```\npub fn match_adapter_with_glob(pattern: &str, model_name: &str) -> Option<()> {\n    // Handle edge cases\n    if pattern.is_empty() || model_name.is_empty() {\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    // Use the glob crate to compile and match the pattern\n    match glob::Pattern::new(pattern) {\n        Ok(glob_pattern) => {\n            // The glob crate's Pattern::matches takes a &str directly\n            if glob_pattern.matches(model_name) {\n                Some(())\n            } else {\n                None\n            }\n        }\n        Err(_) => {\n            // Invalid glob pattern\n            None\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Routing rule matcher for model-to-adapter dispatch.\n//!\n//! Provides pattern matching logic for routing rules: regex/glob patterns\n//! against model names, first-match-wins semantics, and default fallback.\n\nuse crate::config::RoutingRule;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\n/// Compiled routing rule with cached regex for efficient matching.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\nstruct CompiledRule {\n    /// Compiled regex matcher.\n    matcher: Arc<regex::Regex>,\n    /// Adapter to use on match.\n    adapter: String,\n}\n\nimpl CompiledRule {\n    /// Compile a routing rule into an efficient matcher.\n    ///\n    /// Supports both regex patterns (any valid regex) and glob-style patterns:\n    /// - `*` matches any single path segment (non-greedy `[^/]+`)\n    /// - `**` matches zero or more path segments (`.+?` with greedy quantifier)\n    /// - Literal `*` or `**` must be escaped as `\\*` or `\\*\\*`\n    fn from_rule(rule: &RoutingRule) -> Result<Self, regex::Error> {\n        let pattern = &rule.match_model;\n        let adapter = rule.adapter.clone();\n\n        // Convert glob patterns to regex if needed.\n        // If the pattern contains * or ** without proper regex escaping,\n        // treat it as a glob pattern and convert.\n        let regex_pattern = if needs_glob_conversion(pattern) {\n            convert_glob_to_regex(pattern)\n        } else {\n            pattern.clone()\n        };\n\n        let matcher = regex::Regex::new(&regex_pattern)?;\n\n        Ok(CompiledRule {\n            matcher: Arc::new(matcher),\n            adapter,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Test if a model name matches this rule.\n    fn matches(&self, model: &str) -> bool {\n        self.matcher.is_match(model)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Check if a pattern contains glob-style wildcards that need conversion.\n///\n/// Returns true if the pattern appears to be a glob pattern rather than\n/// a well-formed regex. The heuristic checks for:\n/// 1. Regex features: anchors (^$), character classes [], parentheses (),\n///    quantifiers +?{}, alternation |, or the regex wildcard sequence .*\n/// 2. If present, it's a regex pattern - no conversion needed\n/// 3. If absent, but * is present, it's a glob pattern - convert it\nfn needs_glob_conversion(pattern: &str) -> bool {\n    // First, check if it looks like a regex by looking for regex metacharacters.\n    // The key indicator is .* which is \"any character\" in regex but not in glob.\n    let has_regex_features = pattern.contains(|c| {\n        matches!(\n            c,\n            '^' | '$' | '(' | ')' | '[' | ']' | '{' | '}' | '+' | '?' | '|' | '\\\\'\n        )\n    }) || pattern.contains(\".*\");\n\n    if has_regex_features {\n        // Has clear regex features - treat as regex\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    // At this point, we have a simple pattern that might be glob or regex.\n    // If it contains unescaped * (and we already ruled out other regex chars),\n    // treat it as a glob pattern.\n    let chars: Vec<char> = pattern.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        if chars[i] == '\\\\' && i + 1 < chars.len() {\n            // Skip escaped character.\n            i += 2;\n            continue;\n        }\n        if chars[i] == '*' {\n            return true;\n        }\n        i += 1;\n    }\n\n    false\n}\n\n/// Convert glob-style pattern to regex.\n///\n/// Rules:\n/// - `*` alone → `.*` (match anything, catch-all)\n/// - `*` in other contexts → `[^/]+` (match any single segment, no slashes)\n/// - `**` → `.*` (match any characters including slashes, greedy)\n/// - Escaped `\\*` and `\\*\\*` treated literally\n/// - No implicit start anchor for glob patterns (unlike regex patterns)\nfn convert_glob_to_regex(glob: &str) -> String {\n    // Special case: * and ** should match anything (including empty).\n    if glob == \"*\" || glob == \"**\" {\n        return \"^.*$\".to_string();\n    }\n\n    let mut result = String::new();\n    let chars: Vec<char> = glob.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        match chars[i] {\n            '\\\\' => {\n                // Escaped character - pass through the backslash and the character.\n                // This ensures that \\* in the glob becomes \\* in the regex (literal asterisk).\n                if i + 1 < chars.len() {\n                    result.push('\\\\');\n                    result.push(chars[i + 1]);\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    // Trailing backslash - treat literally.\n                    result.push('\\\\');\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            '*' => {\n                // Check for **.\n                if i + 1 < chars.len() && chars[i + 1] == '*' {\n                    // ** matches any characters including slashes.\n                    result.push_str(\".*\");\n                    i += 2;\n                } else {\n                    // * matches any non-slash characters.\n                    result.push_str(\"[^/]+\");\n                    i += 1;\n                }\n            }\n            c => {\n                // Pass through regex metacharacters literally - regex::Regex::new\n                // will handle escaping. We only need to escape backslashes for\n                // the glob conversion.\n                result.push(c);\n                i += 1;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Only add end anchor, not start anchor (glob patterns match substrings).\n    format!(\"{}$\", result)\n}\n\n/// Match a model name against routing rules, returning the adapter to use.\n///\n/// Evaluates rules in order; the first matching rule determines the adapter.\n/// If no rule matches, returns the default adapter.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `model` - The model name to match (e.g., The adapter name to use.\n/// * `None` - No rule matched and default is empty/invalid (caller should handle).\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::routing::match_adapter;\n/// use needle::config::RoutingRule;\n///\n/// let rules = vec![\n///     RoutingRule {\n///         match_model: \"sonnet.*\".to_string(),\n///         adapter: \"claude-print\".to_string(),\n///     },\n///     RoutingRule {\n///         match_model: \"*\".to_string(),\n///         adapter: \"default-adapter\".to_string(),\n///     },\n/// ];\n///\n/// // First rule matches.\n/// assert_eq!(\n///     match_adapter(\"sonnet-4-6\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n///     Some(\"claude-print\".to_string())\n/// );\n///\n/// // Second rule (catch-all) matches.\n/// assert_eq!(\n///     match_adapter(\"other-model\", &rules, \"fallback\"),\n///     Some(\"default-adapter\".to_string())\n/// );\n/// ```\npub fn match_adapter(model: &str, rules: &[RoutingRule], default: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    // Compile rules and test in order (first match wins).\n    for rule in rules {\n        match CompiledRule::from_rule(rule) {\n            Ok(compiled) => {\n                if compiled.matches(model) {\n                    return Some(compiled.adapter.clone());\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                // Log the error but continue with other rules.\n                // Invalid patterns are skipped rather than failing the entire dispatch.\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    pattern = %rule.match_model,\n                    error = %e,\n                    \"invalid routing pattern — skipping rule\"\n                );\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    // No rule matched — use default if provided.\n    if default.is_empty() {\n        None\n    } else {\n        Some(default.to_string())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Match a model name against a single glob pattern using the glob crate.\n///\n/// This is a lower-level function that tests if a glob pattern matches a model name.\n/// It uses the `glob` crate's Pattern type directly for glob-style pattern matching.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `pattern` - Glob pattern to match (e.g., \"claude-*\", \"gpt-*\", \"*\").\n/// * `model_name` - The model name to test against the pattern.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `Some(())` - The pattern (no match).\n/// * Invalid glob pattern: Returns `None` (no match).\n///\n/// # Glob Pattern Syntax\n///\n/// * `*` - Matches any sequence of non-separator characters.\n/// * `**` - Matches any sequence of characters, including path separators.\n/// * `?` - Matches any single non-separator character.\n/// * `[a-z]` - Matches any character in the bracket.\n/// * `[!a-z]` - Matches any character not in the bracket.\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::routing::match_adapter_with_glob;\n///\n/// // Match with wildcard\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-sonnet-4-6\").is_some());\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"claude-opus-4-6\").is_some());\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"claude-*\", \"gpt-4\").is_none());\n///\n/// // Match with double wildcard\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"**\", \"any-model\").is_some());\n///\n/// // Edge cases\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"\", \"model\").is_none());\n/// assert!(match_adapter_with_glob(\"pattern\", \"\").is_none());\n/// ```\npub fn match_adapter_with_glob(pattern: &str, model_name: &str) -> Option<()> {\n    // Handle edge cases\n    if pattern.is_empty() || model_name.is_empty() {\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    // Use the glob crate to compile and match the pattern\n    match glob::Pattern::new(pattern) {\n        Ok(glob_pattern) => {\n            // The glob crate's Pattern::matches takes a &str directly\n            if glob_pattern.matches(model_name) {\n                Some(())\n            } else {\n                None\n            }\n        }\n        Err(_) => {\n            // Invalid glob pattern\n            None\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// This is a basic check that doesn't attempt to\n/// distinguish between glob and regex patterns - it just reports whether\n/// the pattern contains wildcard characters.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `pattern` - The pattern string to check.\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// * `true` if the pattern contains `*` or `**`.\n/// * `false` otherwise.\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```\n/// use needle::routing::is_glob_pattern;\n///\n/// // Glob patterns with wildcards\n/// assert!(is_glob_pattern(\"*\"));\n/// assert!(is_glob_pattern(\"**\"));\n/// assert!(is_glob_pattern(\"gpt-*\"));\n/// assert!(is_glob_pattern(\"test/**\"));\n///\n/// // Non-glob patterns (no wildcards)\n/// assert!(!is_glob_pattern(\"exact-match\"));\n/// assert!(!is_glob_pattern(\"gpt-4\"));\n/// assert!(!is_glob_pattern(\"claude-sonnet\"));\n/// ```\npub fn is_glob_pattern(pattern: &str) -> bool {\n    pattern.contains('*')\n}\n\n/// Check if a pattern contains glob-style wildcards that need conversion.\n///\n/// Returns true if the pattern appears to be a glob pattern rather than\n/// a well-formed regex. The heuristic checks for:\n/// 1. Regex features: anchors (^$), character classes [], parentheses (),\n///    quantifiers +?{}, alternation |, or the regex wildcard sequence .*\n/// 2. If present, it's a regex pattern - no conversion needed\n/// 3. If absent, but * is present, it's a glob pattern - convert it\nfn needs_glob_conversion(pattern: &str) -> bool {\n    // First, check if it looks like a regex by looking for regex metacharacters.\n    // The key indicator is .* which is \"any character\" in regex but not in glob.\n    let has_regex_features = pattern.contains(|c| {\n        matches!(\n            c,\n            '^' | '$' | '(' | ')' | '[' | ']' | '{' | '}' | '+' | '?' | '|' | '\\\\'\n        )\n    }) || pattern.contains(\".*\");\n\n    if has_regex_features {\n        // Has clear regex features - No implicit start anchor for glob patterns (unlike regex patterns)\nfn convert_glob_to_regex(glob: &str) -> String {\n    // Special case: * and ** should match anything (including empty).\n    if glob == \"*\" || glob == \"**\" {\n        return \"^.*$\".to_string();\n    }\n\n    let mut result = String::new();\n    let chars: Vec<char> = glob.chars().collect();\n    let mut i = 0;\n\n    while i < chars.len() {\n        match chars[i] {\n            '\\\\' => {\n                // Escaped character - regex::Regex::new\n                // will handle escaping. &str) -> Option<()> {\n    // Handle edge cases\n    if pattern.is_empty() || model_name.is_empty() {\n        return None;\n    }\n\n    // Use the glob crate to compile and match the pattern\n    match glob::Pattern::new(pattern) {\n        Ok(glob_pattern) => {\n            // The glob crate's Pattern::matches takes a &str directly\n            if glob_pattern.matches(model_name) {\n                Some(())\n            } else {\n                None\n            }\n        }\n        Err(_) => {\n            // Invalid glob pattern\n            None\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n//
